what_it_does: Graph analytics and scientific computing often use sparse data — arrays where most entries are zero — and accessing them requires following chains of index pointers (for example, first look up which column index to use, then use that index to fetch the actual value). These pointer chains cause the CPU to wait repeatedly for data from main memory (DRAM — the large but slow off-chip storage) because each step depends on the result of the previous one, and there is no locality to exploit. Magellan is a compiler technique — the compiler is the tool that translates human-readable code into machine instructions — that analyzes nested loops to detect and map out these multi-step pointer chains automatically. It then inserts extra instructions that tell the hardware to start fetching the data early (prefetching), hiding the memory wait time behind useful computation. The analysis spans loop boundaries so it can look several loop iterations ahead. This is from the abstract only.
